sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features

items.q: Fill up: The adverse-effects mnemonic printed for acetaldehyde/alcohol injury is ______.
items.exp: 'mnemonic : HESST' — Hypoxia, Endoplasmic reticulum stress, Superoxide, ↓SAM/↑SAH, Toxic effect of acetaldehyde. (Book p1027)

items.q: HESST — match — 1) Hypoxia 2) Endoplasmic reticulum stress 3) Superoxide … A) Mallory hyaline bodies B) Reactive oxygen species produced by Cyt P2E1 C) Mitochondrial injury in zone 3 (centrilobular hepatocyte)
items.exp: Hypoxia: mitochondrial injury in Zone 3 (centrilobular); ER stress: Mallory hyaline bodies; Superoxide: ROS produced by Cyt P2E1. (Book p1027)

items.q: '↓SAM / ↑SAH' in the HESST list is linked to which factor labelled the most important pathogenic factor, and which drug is given as its Rx?
items.exp: '↓SAM/↑SAH : ↑ TNFα most important pathogenic factor' and 'Rx : Pentoxifylline'. (Book p1027)

items.q: Fill up the chain printed for the toxic effect of acetaldehyde: ↑ NADH → ↓ ______ → ______ gut.
items.exp: 'Toxic effect of acetaldehyde : ↑ NADH → ↓ glutathione → leaky gut'. (Book p1027)

items.q: Match — 1) Left image 2) Right image … A) Centrilobular necrosis, balloon degeneration, hepatocyte Mallory bodies B) Eosinophilic body inside hepatocyte: Mallory's hyaline bodies (endoplasmic reticulum stress)
items.exp: Left caption: 'Eosinophilic body inside hepatocyte : Mallory's hyaline bodies (Endoplasmic reticulum stress)'. Right: 'Centrilobular necrosis, Balloon degeneration hepatocyte Mallory bodies'. (Book p1027)

items.q: Under the right micrograph, fatty liver disease is defined by fat in what proportion of hepatocytes, and what does fat pushing the nucleus to the periphery denote?
items.exp: 'Fat in >5% Hepatocytes : Fatty liver disease. Fat pushes nucleus to periphery : macronodular.' (printed wording is macronodular). (Book p1027)

items.q: Laboratory features of alcoholic hepatitis — what is the first bullet and what enzyme range is given?
AST:ALT ratio — match — 1) > 2 : 1 2) > 3 : 1 … A) Highly suggestive of alcoholic hepatitis B) Likely alcoholic hepatitis
items.exp: '>2:1 Likely Alcoholic hepatitis; >3:1 Highly suggestive of Alcoholic hepatitis'. (Book p1027)

items.q: Judge the remaining lab bullets: I S. albumin is a significant marker (positive acute-phase reactant). II PT/INR is raised. III MCV is raised (macrocytosis).
opts: I false; II and III true
I and II true, III false
I true; II and III false
items.exp: 'S. Albumin : Not significant (Negative acute phase reactant)'; 'PT/INR : ↑'; 'MCV ↑ : macrocytosis'. (Book p1027)

items.q: Thiamine depletion in alcoholics is drawn as inhibiting (−) two reactions. Which pair?
opts: Pyruvate → Acyl-CoA (blocked) and the transketolase reaction
items.exp: 'Thiamine depletion (−) (−) → Pyruvate ✗→ Acyl-CoA ; Transketolase Reaction' (printed Acyl-CoA; the physiological product is acetyl-CoA). (Book p1027)

items.q: Clinical features listed on this page — which is NOT printed?
items.exp: Clinical features: Jaundice; P/A Soft, Painful; Hepatomegaly. (Book p1027)
